title: Teaching the Bible
summary: How to teach God's Word effectively in Sunday school, Bible study groups and classes: the teacher's calling, how people learn, planning lessons, teaching children, youth and adults, and leading discussion.
description: God has given teachers to the church to build up His people. This course is for Sunday school teachers, Bible study leaders, youth workers and parents. It explains the calling and responsibility of teaching, how people learn, how to plan a clear Bible lesson with aims and activities, how to teach different age groups, and how to lead discussion, ask good questions and assess learning.
objectives: Understand the biblical calling and responsibility of teachers
Apply principles of how people learn
Plan Bible lessons with clear aims and structure
Adapt teaching for children, youth and adults
outcomes: Explain James 3:1 and the teacher's responsibility
Write clear lesson aims for knowledge, attitude and action
Teach a Bible story to children with age-appropriate methods
Ask open questions and lead a group discussion well

modules.title: Called to Teach
modules.intro: Teaching is a gift and a serious responsibility. This week we study the teacher's calling and character.

lessons.title: Teaching in Scripture
lessons.body:
God commanded Israel to teach His words to their children "diligently" (Deuteronomy 6:7). Ezra taught the law (Ezra 7:10). Jesus was called "Teacher" (Rabbi, Master) more than any other title, and "the people were astonished at his doctrine: For he taught them as one having authority" (Matthew 7:28-29).

The Great Commission includes "teaching them to observe all things" (Matthew 28:20). Christ gave "pastors and teachers" to the church (Ephesians 4:11), and teaching is listed among spiritual gifts (Romans 12:7).

Teaching is how faith is passed from one generation to the next (2 Timothy 2:2; Psalm 78:4-7).

lessons.title: A serious responsibility
lessons.body:
"My brethren, be not many masters [teachers], knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation [stricter judgement]" (James 3:1). Teachers influence how others understand God; false teaching causes great harm (2 Peter 2:1).

This is not meant to frighten us away, but to make us careful: to study, to teach only what Scripture teaches, and to admit when we do not know.

Jesus warned that causing "one of these little ones which believe in me" to stumble is very serious (Matthew 18:6). Those who teach children carry a special trust.

lessons.title: The teacher's character
lessons.body:
Paul told Titus to be "a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, Sound speech" (Titus 2:7-8). People learn more from who we are than from what we say.

The Lord's servant must be "apt to teach, patient, In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves" (2 Timothy 2:24-25).

Good teachers love their learners (1 Thessalonians 2:8), prepare faithfully, keep learning, pray for each learner by name, and live what they teach. For those working with children and young people, safeguarding matters: never be alone with a child behind closed doors, follow church policies, and report concerns.

terms.def: One gifted and called to explain God's Word so others understand and obey.
A Jewish teacher; a title often given to Jesus.
A Spirit-given ability to explain truth clearly (Romans 12:7).
The greater accountability of teachers (James 3:1).
Being an example that matches one's teaching (Titus 2:7).
Practices that protect children and vulnerable people from harm.

modules.title: How People Learn
modules.intro: Good teachers understand learners. This week we study principles of learning from Scripture and experience.

lessons.title: Jesus the master teacher
lessons.body:
Jesus taught with great variety:

- **Stories**: parables from farming, fishing and family life (Matthew 13).
- **Questions**: "Whom say ye that I am?" (Matthew 16:15). He asked more than 300 questions in the Gospels.
- **Object lessons**: a child (Matthew 18:2), a coin (22:19), a fig tree (Mark 11:20-21).
- **Experience**: sending disciples out and debriefing.
- **Repetition**: key truths repeated in different ways.
- **Starting where people were**: the Samaritan woman's water jar; Nicodemus's question.

Jesus always connected truth to life and called for a response.

lessons.title: Principles of learning
lessons.body:
People learn best when:

- **They are actively involved**: discussing, writing, doing, not just listening.
- **Truth connects to life**: "How does this matter for me?"
- **Teaching moves from known to unknown**: building on what they already know.
- **Several senses are used**: hearing, seeing, doing. People remember more of what they do than of what they only hear.
- **There is repetition and review**: "precept upon precept; line upon line" (Isaiah 28:10).
- **They feel safe and valued**, free to ask questions.
- **They practise**: obedience deepens understanding (John 7:17).

The Spirit is the true Teacher (John 14:26). Pray for learners to understand.

lessons.title: Different learners
lessons.body:
Learners differ. Some prefer listening, some reading, some discussion, some hands-on activity. Some think quickly; others need time. Some read easily; others are not literate.

Paul adapted to his hearers (1 Corinthians 9:22). Teachers should vary methods: stories, questions, pictures, drama, songs, memory work, small-group tasks.

In many Nigerian churches, classes include people with very different levels of education. Use simple language, oral methods such as storytelling and repetition, and pair stronger readers with others. Never shame anyone for not knowing. "Knowledge puffeth up, but charity edifieth" (1 Corinthians 8:1).

terms.def: A story from ordinary life that teaches a spiritual truth.
Teaching using a physical object to illustrate truth.
Learning by participating, not only listening.
Building new learning on what learners already understand.
Repeating key truths to help them stick.
Learning through hearing, telling, repeating and memorising, especially for non-readers.

modules.title: Planning a Bible Lesson
modules.intro: A well-planned lesson helps learners understand and obey. This week we learn to set aims and structure a lesson.

lessons.title: Setting aims
lessons.body:
Begin with the Bible passage and its main point (study it as in the preaching course: observe, interpret, apply). Then set **aims** for your learners:

- **Know**: What should they understand? (e.g. "Learners will explain why David trusted God against Goliath.")
- **Feel**: What attitude should grow? (e.g. "Learners will feel confident that God is with them in fear.")
- **Do**: What should they do? (e.g. "Learners will pray about one fear this week.")

Clear aims keep the lesson focused and show what to assess. Ask: "If they remember one thing, what should it be?"

lessons.title: Hook, Book, Look, Took
lessons.body:
A simple lesson structure:

1. **Hook**: catch attention and raise the need, with a question, story, picture or activity connected to life.
2. **Book**: study the Bible passage: read it, tell it, explain it, ask questions about it.
3. **Look**: look at the general truth and how it applies to life today.
4. **Took**: help each learner decide what they will take away and do this week.

This follows Jesus' pattern of connecting to life, teaching truth and calling for response. Plan the time for each part, and end with prayer.

lessons.title: Methods and materials
lessons.body:
Choose methods that fit your aims and learners:

- **Storytelling**: tell Bible stories vividly, especially for children and oral learners.
- **Questions and discussion**: for youth and adults.
- **Drama and role-play**: act out a story or a life situation.
- **Visual aids**: maps, pictures, objects, a chalkboard or flip chart.
- **Memory verses** and songs.
- **Small-group tasks**: groups study different parts of a passage and report back.
- **Crafts and games** for children, always connected to the lesson.

Use low-cost local materials. A good teacher with a Bible and a story can teach anywhere.

terms.def: A clear statement of what learners should know, feel or do.

modules.title: Teaching Different Ages
modules.intro: Children, young people and adults learn differently. This week we study each group and how to lead discussion.

lessons.title: Teaching children
lessons.body:
Jesus welcomed children: "Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me" (Matthew 19:14). Timothy knew the Scriptures "from a child" (2 Timothy 3:15).

Children learn best through stories, repetition, songs, movement and concrete objects. Their attention span is short, so change activity often.

Tips: tell Bible stories as true history; focus on one main truth; use simple words; let children act and respond; teach memory verses; love them and know their names. Present the gospel simply and clearly, but never pressure children to make decisions to please the teacher. Partner with parents, who are children's main teachers (Deuteronomy 6:7).

lessons.title: Teaching youth and adults
lessons.body:
**Teenagers** are asking big questions about identity, purpose, relationships and doubt. They need honest answers, discussion, and adults who listen. Daniel and his friends stood firm as young men (Daniel 1:8); Paul told Timothy, "Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example" (1 Timothy 4:12). Involve them in serving.

**Adults** bring experience and want teaching that is relevant and practical. They learn well through discussion, case studies and connecting Scripture to work, family and society. Respect their experience; let them teach one another (Titus 2:3-5).

All ages need the same gospel, taught at their level.

lessons.title: Leading discussion and assessing learning
lessons.body:
Good questions open discussion:

- **Observation**: What happened? Who said what?
- **Interpretation**: Why did he say that? What does this teach about God?
- **Application**: How does this apply to us? What will you do?

Ask **open questions** (not yes/no), wait for answers, affirm contributions, gently correct errors, and keep the group on the passage. Do not let one person dominate.

Assess learning by asking learners to retell the story, explain the main point, recite memory verses, or report back next week on what they did. The goal is not just knowledge but changed lives: "the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart" (1 Timothy 1:5).

A question that cannot be answered with yes or no.

assignments.title: A full lesson plan
assignments.prompt: Write a complete Bible lesson plan for a class of your choice (children, youth or adults). Include the passage, main point, know-feel-do aims, Hook-Book-Look-Took sections with timings, methods, questions, and how you will assess learning.

assignments.title: Reflecting on teaching
assignments.prompt: Teach your lesson (or observe a teacher). Reflect on what worked, how learners responded, and what you would change, using the principles of this course.
